raw_response:
My whole life I have farmed this land in Quzhou. My mother farmed it, and her mother before her. I do not read, and I do not go to meetings about new methods. I know what the soil here wants, and I know what the market buys. There is no question in my mind what I will plant.

I will grow winter wheat on my 6 mu, same as every year. I put it in the ground in October after the sorghum harvest smell has gone from the air, and I bring it in June. Then right away I plant summer corn — everyone here plants corn, it goes in fast after the wheat comes out and the machine has turned the soil over. The corn is out by late September. Two crops, same land, every year. That is how it is done here.

For wheat I buy from the seed shop in town, the improved kind they always have — not old seeds, those don't yield enough to be worth it. For corn I always buy hybrid. My neighbor's son told me years ago that hybrid corn makes much more. He was right. I have used hybrid ever since.

I apply fertilizer the same as always. I put compound fertilizer down before planting, and I top-dress urea when the plants start growing tall. I water when I must — wheat needs water badly in spring. For corn the rains usually help but I pump twice to be safe. I spray for bugs and disease when I see trouble coming.

I do not experiment. My land gives me about 450 jin of wheat per mu and 550 jin of corn. That is enough.
